6805 bearing support

Independent assembly · 4 mm wall · Existing 40 mm travel screw + bearing ring

100%

Remove the front locknuts and withdraw the holder bolts rearward. Slide the support module off the motor shaft and lift it clear before removing the separate motor screws. The screw and bearing leave the holder from its motor-facing recess. Loosen the coupling first.

The bearing carries axial load into the wall. The existing D-shaft clamp remains accessible through the open holder.

6805
4mm
30.3mm
Rear

Outward bosses and a continuous bearing seat

The 6805 sits in a recess on the motor-facing side of the holder. Feed the threaded end of the screw through the bearing and the holder from the motor side; the printed shoulder rests against the inner race. The front lip of the holder supports the outer race. Four outward mounting bosses sit outside the bearing-seat body on a 52 × 31 mm pattern. Full-depth columns and M3×45 steel through-bolts replace the thin ribs. Front-facing locknuts and washers are accessible without reaching into the bearing housing. The NEMA17 has its own four screws.

Existing screw + bearing ring

The original helix, D bore and bolt/nut pockets are retained. The added ring has a Ø24.9 mm journal and Ø27 mm shoulder, occupying X22.3–31.3 mm. The coupling split stays open through the added material.

1 mm shorter holder

The holder projects 30.3 mm from the front of the 4 mm wall, reduced from 31.3 mm. The motor and screw keep their existing relative positions. The wall is now 64 × 52 × 4 mm, retaining its central NEMA17 holes and adding the external holder pattern. The holder matches the revised T8 Z versions; the other actuator types remain unchanged.

Motor-facing recess

The bearing recess is Ø37.2 mm. Its forward lip contacts only the outer race, with 0.1 mm nominal axial clearance. The rear bearing-loading path stays clear. The 360° lip is uninterrupted by screw-access slots. Four M3×45 bolts, eight washers and four DIN 985 locknuts tie the front plate to the wall. Thrust toward the screw tip passes into the wall; reverse-direction retention relies on the coupling.

Geometry checks

Loading validation…

All 41 sampled exploded-assembly poses are free of solid intersections. Continuous insertion envelopes verify rear bolt loading. Separate checks verify the complete mounting columns, continuous bearing lip and positive abutments through the washers, bolt heads and wall. The bearing leaves from the motor side; it never passes through the holder’s front lip. Sampling checks rigid clearances, not installation forces.

Designed around the earlier 1 lb (4.45 N) static input. The load path is positively retained toward the screw tip; this is still a prototype without a physically tested load rating. CAD checks do not establish PETG creep life, fatigue or vibration resistance. Bearing internals are reference envelopes. This bearing does not prevent back-driving when the motor is unpowered.

Geometry report · Assembly pose report

Assembly and hardware

  1. Seat the 6805 in the recess on the motor-facing side of the holder.
  2. Feed the screw’s threaded end through the bearing and holder from the motor side, until its shoulder reaches the bearing’s inner race. Fit the original clamp nut and bolt loosely.
  3. Attach the motor to the 4 mm wall with four M3×10 screws, then slide the support module onto the shaft. Load the four M3×45 holder bolts and rear washers from behind the wall. Fit the exposed front washers and M3 locknuts. Verify the motor accepts 6 mm screw engagement.
  4. Gently seat the screw toward its tip until the outer race rests against the housing lip, then tighten the coupling in that seated position without preloading the motor shaft. Check free rotation before loading.

Print the wall flat; print the holder with its front face on the bed and columns upward. An actual P2S / Generic PETG / 0.20 mm slice with automatic supports enabled generates zero support extrusion for the holder (slice report). Check actual PETG fits before loading.
